subject: Consolidate renewal into annual schedule + early burst request
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@novascale.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal planning: annualize + Q1 burst ask

Hi Ben / Marissa,

Quick context — our renewal is up mid-February and the team is hoping to simplify the contract cadence. We'd like to move from the current quarterly cadence into a single annual agreement if possible. The drivers: finance prefers one invoice, and our product team needs a predictable pool for forecasting.

Two asks up front:
- Can Redwood consolidate our current staggered renewals into one annual term that co-terms us at Feb 1?
- We have a short-term burst need for Jan-Feb (estimated additional 600k tokens/day). Can you propose an early-burst bucket we can draw against?

I've attached our Q4 usage report to make the numbers concrete. Happy to jump on a quick call this week to go over options.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Li
CTO, NovaScale
[Attachment: usage_report_Q42026.csv (CSV)]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@novascale.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-21T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: annualize + Q1 burst ask

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear ask and the usage file.

Short answer: yes, we can consolidate you onto a single annual term and create a one-time early-burst bucket for Jan-Feb. To give you concrete options, I'll outline two approaches and we can pick the one that maps to NovaScale's risk profile: 

Option A — Annual + Reserved Burst (recommended):
- One-year term starting Feb 1, annual billing.
- Reserved baseline = your trailing 3-month average * 1.1 (to cover typical growth).
- Early-burst credit: pre-purchase a 2-month burst pool billed up-front at a discounted rate (we can do 15% off pro-rated unit price).
- Auto-renew can be enabled; we’ll include a 60-day renewal notice window.

Option B — Multi-year (2x) with staged ramp:
- 2-year term, lower unit price, with staged minimums that ramp 25% year-over-year.
- Burst as overage credits (no pre-pay) but with guaranteed capacity SLA for short windows.

I attached a draft amendment that shows the mechanics for Option A (term language + burst calculation). If this looks good, I'll loop in Neha from Finance for invoicing and Tessa from Customer Success for onboarding and burst capacity playbook.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow (Dec 22) at 10am PT?

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_draft_amendment_v1.pdf (PDF)]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Sarah Li <sarah.li@novascale.io>
Date: 2026-12-22T13:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: annualize + Q1 burst ask

Thanks Ben and Sarah — good summary. A couple of practical notes from a deployment/ops perspective: 

- Canary capacity: For the early-burst window, we'll reserve a small warm pool (10% of burst) so cold-start latency doesn't impact NovaScale. That will be included in the pre-pay calculation.
- Auto-renew toggles: If NovaScale wants auto-renew turned on, we'll include a 30/60/90-day notice tier mapping so you can choose how much runway for negotiations you want.
- Escalation path: add an SLO exception clause for one 24-hour window during the burst where we commit to negotiated mitigation credits if throughput drops below the agreed threshold.

Pricing note: I put two example numbers into a quick table and uploaded it to the thread (pricing_comparison_table.xlsx). Ben — if NovaScale is leaning toward annual with pre-paid burst, I'd recommend the 15% burst discount to make the upfront commitment easier to justify to finance.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Strategy

[Attachment: pricing_comparison_table.xlsx (XLSX)]
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@novascale.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-24T08:41:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: annualize + Q1 burst ask

Thanks — the options look fair. A couple quick clarifications: 
1) We prefer a single annual invoice (Option A).
2) For the burst, can you confirm the draw-down mechanics and whether unused pre-paid burst credits roll forward or expire? Our procurement will push back if credits expire the same day.
3) SOC2 evidence: our compliance team wants your current SOC2 report and an indemnity confirmation for data residency. Can Neha lead finance/security coordination?

If those answers look good I can sign the amendment quickly — Feb 1 start date aligns with our fiscal planning.

—Sarah

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-28T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: annualize + Q1 burst ask — next steps

Sarah — great, glad Option A works. To confirm next steps and responsibilities: 

1) Contract: We'll update the draft amendment to reflect: Feb 1 start, one-year term, annual invoice, 2-month pre-paid burst (draw-down model), 15% discount on burst units, and 60-day auto-renew notice. I'll circulate the updated PDF by EOD tomorrow.

2) Credits mechanics: unused burst credits will roll forward for up to 90 days; after that they expire. We'll put the 90-day roll-forward into Section 3 of the amendment per your procurement ask.

3) Compliance & finance: Neha (cc'd) will share SOC2 documentation and confirm invoicing path. Neha — can you confirm whether NovaScale needs a PO on the invoice?

4) Onboarding & ops: Tessa (cc'd) will schedule a pre-burst runbook call for the first week of Jan (30min) to validate warm pool size and KV-caching strategy.

5) Signature flow: We'll send a DocuSign link with the amendment. HubSpot deal NS-2026-115 will be updated to reflect the annualized term and the burst addendum.

Thanks all — I'll follow up with the updated amendment and the DS link.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
